title: Paravalvular leak closure
scope: Generic class mechanism in representative anatomy. The anatomy, device shape and positions shown are representative of this class; they are not measured on a specific patient or population, and not a specific product. Schematic, not to scale; poses do not predict clinical fit, deformation, performance or flow.
stageLabel: Schematic · representative anatomy · not to scale
attribution: Whole-heart context adapted from Toronto Heart Atlas by Azad Mashari, Joshua Qua Hiansen, Mini Pakkal, Eitan Aziza, Ryan Ramos, Sachin Khargie and Massimiliano Meineri (CC BY 4.0). Display smoothing, vessel continuations and edits for readability are modifications. Detailed tissue shells, defects, device shapes and positions are representative schematics. They are not measured on a specific patient or population, and are not segmented tissue or clinical simulations.

designs.label: Generic peri-prosthetic plug
designs.summary: A synthetic channel lies beside a generic prosthetic cuff. No measured prosthesis or defect is represented.

states.label: Peri-prosthetic channel
states.note: The synthetic channel is outside the prosthetic cuff, separate from the central valve opening.

states.label: Plug above the channel
states.note: The generic plug is shown apart from the channel to expose its relationship. This is not a procedural instruction.

states.label: Plug within the channel
states.note: The plug occupies the representative peri-cuff channel. No sealing, flow or clinical result is predicted.

views.label: Whole heart
views.title: Locate the treatment region
views.lesson: Use the highlighted region to orient the enlarged views.

views.label: Left chambers
views.title: See the valve between the chambers
views.lesson: The left atrium and left ventricle of a real heart are opened along their long axis. Seen from above the valve, the gap beside the prosthetic cuff is separate from the valve opening.

views.label: Mechanism section
views.title: See the tissue–device relationship
views.lesson: Distinguish the peri-cuff channel from the prosthesis central opening; the generic plug belongs outside the cuff.

views.label: Oblique detail
views.title: Understand depth and attachment
views.lesson: An oblique view separates the near surface, device and supporting tissue.

views.label: Face view
views.title: Look along the opening
views.lesson: The face view complements the section. All poses and proportions are representative, not measured.

location.label: TREATMENT LOCATION
location.body: The highlighted region locates this class in the heart. The marker is enlarged for orientation.

channel.label: PERI-PROSTHETIC CHANNEL
channel.body: This deliberately synthetic opening lies outside the cuff. It is not a native leaflet coaptation gap.

cuff.label: PROSTHETIC CUFF
cuff.body: A generic prosthetic cuff separates the central valve opening from the peri-cuff channel.

opening.label: CENTRAL VALVE OPENING
opening.body: The central prosthetic valve opening is separate from the channel targeted by the generic plug.

device.label: GENERIC CHANNEL PLUG
device.body: The plug occupies a representative channel. Position does not imply sealing, safety, compatibility or flow reduction.

region_atrium.label: LEFT ATRIUM
region_atrium.body: The left atrium sits above the valve. Its shape comes from a real heart, opened along its long axis.

region_ventricle.label: LEFT VENTRICLE
region_ventricle.body: The left ventricle sits below the valve. Its cavity and wall shape come from the same real heart.

region_aorta.label: AORTIC ROOT
region_aorta.body: The aortic root sits beside the front leaflet of the mitral valve and helps with orientation.

region_cuff.label: PROSTHETIC CUFF
region_cuff.body: A generic replacement valve sits in the mitral ring. Its sewing cuff is shown cut along the section.

region_channel.label: PERI-PROSTHETIC CHANNEL
region_channel.body: This representative gap lies between the cuff and the surrounding tissue, outside the valve opening.

region_device.label: GENERIC CHANNEL PLUG
region_device.body: The plug sits in the gap beside the cuff. Its shape is representative, not a specific product. Its position does not imply sealing.
